threads.body: [General] Both this customizer and `SpringWebClientInstrumentationSpringBoot4AutoConfiguration.otelWebClientCustomizer()` lose the duplicate-filter check previously performed by `addFilter`. Customizing a builder that already contains a tracing filter, including one obtained from an instrumented client's `mutate()`, now appends another `WebClientTracingFilter`; repeated customization keeps growing the filter chain. `WebClientBeanPostProcessor` only avoids adding its own filter and does not remove existing duplicates. Preserve the presence check in both customizers, preferably by sharing the post-processor's existing check. Add customizer coverage for an already-instrumented builder and repeated customization; the new post-processor test does not exercise these paths.

replies.body: Fixed in 5fa4ea01d06c103260063c8d4ea0cd46d20308e9. Both Boot customizers and the bean postprocessor now share the starter's internal presence-check/install helper. Existing filters remain untouched, and the shared customizer tests cover preinstalled filters, mutated instrumented clients, and repeated customization. The public library API remains factory-only.

@copilot Update this PR directly with one scoped correction to preserve the Spring Boot starter's duplicate-filter detection across all automatic configuration paths. Copilot review 5631530461 identified a real omission: SpringWebfluxInstrumentationAutoConfiguration.otelWebClientCustomizer and SpringWebClientInstrumentationSpringBoot4AutoConfiguration.otelWebClientCustomizer now unconditionally append createFilter(), whereas their previous addFilter calls checked for an existing WebClientTracingFilter. WebClientBeanPostProcessor still checks independently, but cannot remove duplicates already introduced by either customizer.

Keep the requested public API changes exactly as delivered: WebFlux client createFilter/createFilterAndRegisterReactorHook factories with no list-mutating helpers or compatibility aliases, and Ratpack wrap(HttpClient). Preserve duplicate detection in the starter by reusing or extracting its existing internal presence-check/install helper for both Boot 2/3 and Boot 4 customizers as well as the postprocessor. Do not put duplicate detection back into the library factory. Existing filters and their configuration should remain untouched, and repeated automatic customization must not grow the filter chain. Add focused tests for a builder that already has a manually installed filter, a builder derived from an instrumented client's mutate(), and repeated customization, covering the supported Boot customizer variants. Run narrow formatting and relevant tests. Do not change server APIs or unrelated code. Do not update the PR title or description; the coordinator handles metadata.

replies.body: Preserved the duplicate-filter check with a shared starter helper used by both Boot customizers and the post-processor, and added coverage for preinstalled filters, `mutate()`, and repeated customization. Focused Spring Boot 2/3 and 4 tests passed. Commit: `5fa4ea01`.

Updated in `15821fa8`: both Boot customizers now install via `builder.filter(createFilter())`; duplicate detection remains local to the bean post-processor, and customizer deduplication tests were removed.

Keep the other installation and non-WebClient tests. The desired result is one clear duplicate-filter test for an explicitly instrumented client, not two ways to exercise the same presence check.

Preserve the settled API changes and behavior: WebFlux factory-only client API, Ratpack wrap(HttpClient), no compatibility aliases, no duplicate checks in the Boot customizers, and the retained bean postprocessor presence check. Do not restore customizer deduplication based on prior review history. Run narrow formatting and the relevant focused tests. Do not change the PR title or description; the coordinator handles metadata.

threads.body: In retrospect I think we should have used `instrument` (or maybe `confugure`) everywhere since it really doesn't tell how exactly the instrumenation is performed. To me `wrap` means that some sort of decorator is being added around the original object. Here the instrumenation really creates a copy of the original client and adds some interceptors which isn't exactly wrapping. I guess this isn't super important, idk maybe we'll switch to wrapping in the future.
